approaches.approach: Standalone .mjs that reads the store JSON directly and re-implements the small grouping in plain JS. It has its own Entry typedef comment and its own path scrub.
approaches.tradeoff: No build or TS step, matches the other _repo/scripts/*.mjs, and tests run under plain `node --test`. The grouping logic can drift from trophy/hooks/failures.ts (targetOf), so keep the key shape explicit and cite failures.ts in a comment.

approaches.approach: Import trophy/hooks/failures.ts (targetOf, foldRows) from the script.
approaches.tradeoff: No drift, but it needs TS type-stripping. Node version support is unverified, and the repo scripts are plain mjs. It also couples a repo tool to a plugin's internals.

approaches.tradeoff: Cleaner contract, but it changes a plugin (behaviour change, bump, mod rules) and is far beyond the card.

result.chose: Standalone .mjs (approach 1). It finds the store by globbing ~/.claude/plugins/store/trophy_*.json, takes the file whose JSON has trophy.failures, prefers the non-inline one, and honours --from. It also takes --backlog <path> and --store <dir> so the test can use a temp copy.

The trophy_inline-*.json file has no failures key and the store dir has other plugins' files, so the script picks files by name and by key, and an absent key means no records, not an error.

Entry shape follows trophy/hooks/failures.ts: ts, day, kind (bug|outcome|report), reason, plugin?, skill?, tool?, version?, cc?, session, local{text?,note?,slug?,subgoal?,path?}. Outcome entries (kind outcome: subgoal_failed or goal_failed) have no plugin or skill and carry the project path in local. They are skipped by default, since they record harness run results, not bugs to file. Only kind bug and report become cards. The planner may flip this.

Card numbering: --write assigns the next free number after the highest N. in the backlog. Re-runs reuse the number found by tag.

decisions.question: What is this task for (intent)?
decisions.chose: Write a repo-only node script that turns the local trophy failure records into one deduplicated backlog card per group, plus a fixture test. Run it once as a dry run on this machine's real records, and close card 179.

decisions.question: What is in scope?
decisions.chose: _repo/scripts/failures-to-backlog.mjs: reads the trophy store file (auto-found under ~/.claude/plugins/store/trophy_*.json, key trophy.failures) or --from <json>; Grouping by plugin · skill/tool · reason · first text line with paths scrubbed; default dry run prints the cards; --write adds or updates one card per group in _repo/docs/backlog.md, keyed by a [fail:<hash>] tag so a re-run updates the count instead of duplicating; _repo/scripts/test-failures-to-backlog.mjs: node:test with fixtures, us

decisions.question: What is out of scope?
decisions.chose: Any network call or telemetry change; Changes to trophy/hooks/*; Version bump; A mod or skill; this is a repo script only; Auto-running the script from a hook; Prompts, ids, paths or session ids in card text; Running --write on the real backlog beyond what the card asks, unless the planner decides it does

decisions.question: Which approach?
decisions.chose: Standalone .mjs (approach 1). It finds the store by globbing ~/.claude/plugins/store/trophy_*.json, takes the file whose JSON has trophy.failures, prefers the non-inline one, and honours --from. It also takes --backlog <path> and --store <dir> so the test can use a temp copy.
decisions.because: It fits the existing scripts and needs no toolchain. It is the smallest change that meets the acceptance criteria. A copy of targetOf is about 10 lines, and the test pins it.

decisions.question: Assumption 1
decisions.chose: The store is verified: ~/.claude/plugins/store/trophy_newkayak12-claude-skills-b50a8464da51.json is a flat JSON object with key 'trophy.failures', an array of 35 Entry records. The trophy_inline-*.json file has no failures key and the store dir has other plugins' files, so the script picks files by name and by key, and an absent key means no records, not an error.

decisions.question: Assumption 2
decisions.chose: Entry shape follows trophy/hooks/failures.ts: ts, day, kind (bug|outcome|report), reason, plugin?, skill?, tool?, version?, cc?, session, local{text?,note?,slug?,subgoal?,path?}. Real records may lack fields (the sample outcome has no plugin and has local.slug '—'), so every field is read defensively.

decisions.question: Assumption 3
decisions.chose: Group key = plugin · (skill|tool) · reason · first non-empty line of local.text or note, scrubbed: absolute and ~ paths become <path>, uuids and long hex ids become <id>, digits are not touched, and the line is truncated to about 120 characters. The [fail:<hash>] tag is a short sha1 over that key, so it is stable across runs. Counts and versions are excluded from the hash.

decisions.question: Assumption 4
decisions.chose: Outcome entries (kind outcome: subgoal_failed or goal_failed) have no plugin or skill and carry the project path in local. They are skipped by default, since they record harness run results, not bugs to file. Only kind bug and report become cards. The planner may flip this.

decisions.question: Assumption 5
decisions.chose: A card follows backlog.md's shape: '**Title**' with Why (count, day range, plugin versions, Claude Code versions, reason, first scrubbed line) and Acceptance, placed in a `### Failure records (auto)` section so --write never touches hand-written cards. Updating a card rewrites only its Why line count and day range, matched by [fail:<hash>]. A card the person edited or closed (deleted) is not recreated unless the failure recurs; that is a limitation, and a deleted tag is not remembered.

decisions.question: Assumption 6
decisions.chose: Card numbering: --write assigns the next free number after the highest N. in the backlog. Re-runs reuse the number found by tag.

decisions.question: Assumption 7
decisions.chose: Dry run prints to stdout only and never writes. The real-record dry run prints scrubbed text only, so the report holds no paths, prompts or ids.

decisions.question: Assumption 8
decisions.chose: Sprint close, committing, and deleting card 179 are the orchestrator's steps; the script does not edit card 179.

F1-AC-2: Given two files both holding the key, one inline, When discovery runs, Then the non-inline file is used.

F1-AC-6: Given a bug record with `local: {}` (no text), When read, Then it is kept, its first line is empty, and it groups under plugin · target · reason · empty line.
F1-AC-7: Given a report record with neither plugin nor skill nor tool, When read, Then the target and plugin fall back to `-` and no exception occurs.
F1-AC-8: Given a record missing `version`, `cc` or `day`, When read, Then the card shows no value for it and the script exits 0.
F1-AC-9: Given a fixture with bug, report, `subgoal_failed` and `goal_failed` entries, When the script runs, Then only bug and report entries are counted and no card mentions an outcome.
F1-AC-10: Given three records with the same plugin, target, reason and first line but different versions, When grouped, Then there is one group with count 3.

F1-AC-14: Given any output, When searched, Then it holds no prompt text, session id or path.
F1-AC-15: Given the same group in two runs with different counts and versions, When tagged, Then the tag is identical.
F1-AC-16: Given two groups differing in any one key part, When tagged, Then their tags differ.
F1-AC-17: Given a tag, When printed, Then it is `[fail:` plus the first 8 hex characters of the sha1 of the key (default - revisit with maintainer).

F1-AC-19: Given `--write` absent and `--backlog` given, When it runs, Then the file is still not written.
